title: Eddie Heywood's rumpled clothes and being dressed by Simmons
summary: Heywood's sloppy dress, and the tailor Simmons took him to.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When did you meet Billie Holiday?

I had just come off the road with Louis Armstrong and I had returned to the Village Vanguard. Well at that time I was a clothes horse, you know, I loved clothes. I had a suit for every day in the week and then some. Sport coats and hats and berets, anything to be different. So I'm on the stand, clean and lean and Eddie Heywood is sitting there on the piano stool in a Howard Suit. Oh a Howard Suit, see costs about $18.00, Thom McCAnn shoes cost about five and he'd wear his tie on and instead of untieing the tie, he would just slip it down and pull it over his head and put it back on his head in the morning. At night when he'd come to work, slip it back up and that knot would be just as greasy and his socks was dropped around his ankles. And hair uncombed; he wore a stocking cap to bed and when he got up, he didn't brush it or get this line off his forehead. His hair would be matted down and people would come to me and ask me for requests. They thought it was my group, you know (laughter). So the young lady liked Eddie so

much, she gave him a shirt -- I think it cost about $50.00. That's more than he had on! (Laughter). You know, so Lem Davis and I took him to our tailor who was Leeds Tailors in Manhattan. We picked out the materials, told him how to cut it and at that time the one piece back was fashionable, you know. And we dressed him up and boy he looked like someone else.
